newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas still pressured late by weather.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas still pressured late by weather.

text.p: NYMEX Hub natgas futures remained pressured late Wednesday in sluggish activity, with sentiment growing more bearish amid mild weather forcasts for next week and ample storage, industry sources said.
At 1400 EST, April was unchanged at $1.865 per million British thermal units, while May was 0.2 cent higher at $1.90. Other months were down by one-half to two cents.

"If March is as warm as February, you could see futures in the $1.50s. No one needs gas and there's still too much in storage," said one East Coast trader, noting 10-day forecasts were calling for mostly above-normal weather.

Traders said expectations for only a modest weekly drawdown in tonight's AGA storage report also were pressuring the complex. A Reuter poll showed most expected a weekly draw in the 80-95 bcf range versus a 64 bcf decline for the same week last year.

Technical traders said futures were likely to remain in recent ranges until clearer signs emerge next week from the March cash. They still pegged April support at $1.80, then in the mid-$1.70s and the contract low of $1.701. Resistance was seen along the down trendline in the $1.90 area, then at $1.935 and $2.04.

In the physical market, March Gulf Coast gas edged up slightly Wednesday to the mid-to-high $1.70s. March Midcon gas also was talked modestly higher in the mid-$1.60s. New York city gate for March was little changed in the $2.10-15 area.
NYMEX said 15,518 Hub contracts traded as of 1340 EST.
NYMEX Permian natgas was still untraded at 1355 EST. March Alberta natgas remained unchanged at $1.15.
On the KCBT, April was still up by one cent at $1.63, while deferreds remained one-half to 1.5 cents higher. The East/West spread narrowed by one cents to 23.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
